stem: Which city became a leading centre of the Italian Renaissance?
explanation: Florence became a major centre of Renaissance art, humanist learning, and patronage.

stem: Renaissance humanists renewed the study of which body of writing?
explanation: Humanists studied Greek and Roman literature, history, and philosophy, adapting classical learning to their own time.

stem: Which family was a prominent patron of artists and scholars in Florence?
explanation: The Medici used wealth and political influence to commission art and support learning in Florence.

stem: Johannes Gutenberg is associated with the spread in western Europe of which technology?
explanation: Gutenberg helped establish movable-metal-type printing in western Europe, making text reproduction more practical.

stem: Where was Gutenberg’s famous Bible printed?
explanation: Gutenberg’s Bible was printed in Mainz in the mid-fifteenth century. It is a major early western European book made with movable metal type.

stem: Which writer authored In Praise of Folly?
explanation: Erasmus wrote In Praise of Folly, a humanist work that satirized social and religious practices.

stem: Who wrote Utopia, published in 1516?
explanation: Thomas More’s Utopia described an imagined society and became a major work of Renaissance humanist writing.

stem: The Prince, a work on political power, was written by whom?
explanation: Machiavelli wrote The Prince, examining how rulers acquire and maintain political power.

stem: Who wrote The Divine Comedy?
explanation: Dante wrote The Divine Comedy in the early fourteenth century. Its use of Italian helped establish the vernacular as a language of major literature.

stem: Which writer is often called an early father of Renaissance humanism?
explanation: Petrarch’s recovery and study of classical Latin works helped shape Renaissance humanist scholarship.

stem: Which work was painted by Leonardo da Vinci in Milan?
explanation: Leonardo painted The Last Supper in Milan. The work depicts Jesus and his disciples at the meal before his arrest.

stem: Who painted the Mona Lisa?
explanation: Leonardo da Vinci painted the Mona Lisa, one of the best-known portraits of the Renaissance.

stem: Which description best fits Renaissance humanism?

options.text: The study of classical learning and human life
The rejection of all ancient writing
The replacement of art by navigation

explanation: Humanism renewed classical study and emphasized education and human capacities. It was not a single political or religious doctrine.

stem: Which artist painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel?
explanation: Michelangelo painted the Sistine Chapel ceiling in Rome for Pope Julius II.

stem: What changed as printing with movable type spread?

options.text: Texts could be reproduced and circulated more widely
Only royal decrees could be printed

explanation: Printing made it easier to reproduce books and arguments, although handwritten manuscripts continued to be used.

stem: Why were vernacular religious texts important during the Reformation?

options.text: They prevented people from reading scripture
They were written only for the papacy
They ended the use of printing
They could reach readers who did not use Latin

explanation: Texts in local languages could reach people beyond the Latin-educated clergy. Printing helped them circulate.

stem: Who painted The School of Athens?
explanation: Raphael painted The School of Athens for the Vatican rooms; it portrays ancient philosophers in an idealized setting.

stem: In which year did Martin Luther’s Ninety-five Theses appear?
explanation: Luther’s Ninety-five Theses date to 1517 and challenged indulgence practices.

stem: The Ninety-five Theses criticized the sale of what?
explanation: Luther criticized indulgences, which were connected to remission of temporal punishment for sin.

stem: Which German city is closely associated with Luther’s early Reformation activity?
explanation: Luther taught in Wittenberg, and the Ninety-five Theses are associated with the city. The exact posting story is debated.

stem: At the Diet of Worms in 1521, Luther was asked to do what?
explanation: Luther was called upon to recant at the Diet of Worms and refused to withdraw his writings.

stem: Which reformer became closely associated with Geneva?
explanation: John Calvin’s ministry and writings were closely connected with Geneva and helped shape Reformed Protestant traditions.

stem: Which English monarch’s government asserted royal supremacy over the Church of England?
explanation: Henry VIII’s government broke with papal authority and established the monarch’s supremacy over the English Church.

stem: What did the Act of Supremacy of 1534 declare?

options.text: The pope became head of Parliament
The English monarch was supreme head of the Church of England
Calvin became head of the English Church

explanation: The 1534 Act of Supremacy established royal authority over the Church of England.

stem: Which council clarified Catholic doctrine during the Catholic Reformation?
explanation: The Council of Trent (1545–1563) clarified Catholic teaching and addressed reform within the Catholic Church.

stem: What helped the Protestant Reformation spread across Europe?

options.text: Printing and local religious and political networks

explanation: Printing aided the spread of reform arguments, while local rulers, communities, and religious networks shaped how they took hold.

stem: Which statement distinguishes the Council of Trent from Luther’s movement?

options.text: Both were meetings led by Luther
Trent was part of Catholic reform; Luther’s movement helped form Protestant churches
Both established royal supremacy in England

explanation: The Council of Trent was part of Catholic reform. Luther’s challenge contributed to the emergence and growth of Protestant churches.

stem: Which development most directly enabled reform arguments to circulate quickly?
explanation: Printing made it easier to reproduce and circulate reform texts, though it was one factor among several.

stem: Who published a heliocentric account of the planetary system in 1543?
explanation: Copernicus’s 1543 work placed the Sun at the centre of the planetary system and treated Earth as a moving planet.

stem: Galileo’s telescopic observations of Jupiter showed that what?

options.text: Some celestial bodies orbit a body other than Earth
Earth is the only centre of motion

explanation: Galileo observed moons orbiting Jupiter. This showed that not every celestial body revolved around Earth.

stem: Which work did Copernicus publish in 1543?
explanation: Copernicus published De revolutionibus in 1543. It presented a mathematical account of a Sun-centred planetary system.

stem: Which astronomer described planetary orbits as ellipses?
explanation: Kepler’s laws described planets moving in elliptical rather than perfect circular orbits.

stem: Newton’s Principia, published in 1687, is associated with which ideas?

options.text: Laws of motion and universal gravitation

explanation: Newton’s Principia set out laws of motion and gravitation, linking the study of earthly and celestial motion.

stem: Which scholar is known for observation-based human anatomy and De humani corporis fabrica?
explanation: Vesalius’s 1543 anatomy work drew on direct observation of the human body and challenged inherited descriptions.

stem: Who explained the circulation of blood through the body?
explanation: Harvey described the circulation of blood in De motu cordis, published in 1628.

stem: Francis Bacon is most closely linked with support for which approach to knowledge?

options.text: The use of astrology to explain anatomy

explanation: Bacon promoted systematic observation and investigation as ways to develop knowledge about nature.

stem: Vasco da Gama reached India by sailing along which route?

options.text: Around the Cape of Good Hope

explanation: Da Gama rounded Africa and reached Calicut in 1498, establishing a Portuguese sea route to the Indian Ocean.

stem: Columbus’s 1492 expedition crossed which ocean while sailing west?
explanation: Columbus crossed the Atlantic while seeking a westward sea route to Asia; he reached Caribbean islands.

stem: Which navigator rounded Africa’s southern cape in 1488?
explanation: Dias rounded Africa’s southern cape in 1488, opening the way for later Portuguese voyages toward the Indian Ocean.

stem: Pedro Álvares Cabral’s 1500 voyage is linked to Portuguese arrival in which present-day country?
explanation: Cabral’s fleet reached the coast of Brazil in 1500 while sailing toward India.

stem: Which statement correctly compares Columbus’s and da Gama’s routes?

options.text: Both sailed around Africa to reach the Caribbean
Columbus sailed around Africa; da Gama crossed the Pacific
Columbus sailed west across the Atlantic; da Gama rounded Africa toward India
Both crossed the Pacific to reach India

explanation: Columbus crossed the Atlantic westward in 1492; da Gama rounded Africa to reach India in 1498.

stem: Why was the Cape of Good Hope important to Portuguese voyages?

options.text: It marked the boundary between England and France
It was the starting point of Columbus’s voyage
It connected the Mediterranean to the Baltic
It gave ships access around Africa into the Indian Ocean

explanation: Rounding the Cape opened an ocean route from the Atlantic toward the Indian Ocean and Asian trade.

stem: The 1494 Treaty of Tordesillas was agreed between which kingdoms?
explanation: Spain and Portugal agreed to the Treaty of Tordesillas in 1494 amid competition over overseas claims.

stem: What did the Treaty of Tordesillas establish?

options.text: A border between France and Germany
A religious settlement between Catholics and Lutherans
A line dividing Spanish and Portuguese overseas claims
A route linking Portugal to India

explanation: The treaty set a line of demarcation for the overseas claims of Spain and Portugal.

stem: Which expedition completed the first circumnavigation of Earth?
explanation: The expedition began under Magellan and returned under Elcano in 1522. Magellan did not complete the return journey.

stem: Who led the surviving crew back to Spain in 1522?
explanation: Elcano led the surviving expedition back to Spain after Magellan’s death in the Philippines.

stem: Where did Magellan die during the circumnavigation expedition?
explanation: Magellan died in the Philippines in 1521; the surviving expedition continued and returned to Spain the following year.

stem: Which year is associated with Cabral’s arrival on the coast of Brazil?
explanation: Cabral’s expedition reached Brazil in 1500 while travelling toward India.

stem: Which explanation best connects printing with the spread of Luther’s challenge?

options.text: Printing itself created Luther’s religious objections
Printing immediately ended Catholic authority throughout Europe
Vernacular texts prevented readers from discussing reform
Printed texts could be reproduced and circulated, carrying arguments beyond Wittenberg

explanation: Printing helped Luther’s arguments reach wider audiences, but it did not create the religious disputes or end church authority at once.

stem: A Florentine family commissions a chapel, sculptures, and scholarly work. Which historical role does this example illustrate?

options.text: A royal ban on public art
The end of civic influence in Italian cities
The replacement of humanist study by navigation
Patronage helped sustain Renaissance art and learning

explanation: Wealthy patrons paid for works and supported scholars. Their support was one condition that allowed Renaissance cultural activity to flourish.

stem: Which statement best describes the religious changes of the sixteenth century?

options.text: The Reformation united all western Christians under one church
The Council of Trent established Protestant churches
Protestant movements grew, while the Catholic Church also undertook reforms
The Catholic Church ended its institutional role in Europe

explanation: The Reformation produced Protestant churches, while the Council of Trent formed part of Catholic reform. These were related but distinct developments.

stem: Why did vernacular printing matter to religious debate?

options.text: It made some texts accessible to readers who did not read Latin and helped circulate them
It ensured every reader interpreted scripture in the same way
It restricted religious debate to universities

explanation: Local-language texts could reach readers beyond the Latin-educated clergy. Printing helped circulate them, though access and interpretation still varied.

stem: Which account of the Atlantic system is historically defensible?

options.text: It created equal benefits and political power for every connected society
It involved European merchants but no African or American communities
It ended the forced movement of people across the Atlantic
It connected regions through trade and settlement, as well as conquest and forced migration

explanation: Atlantic connections included commerce and settlement, but also conquest, unequal power, and the forced migration of Africans.

stem: Which description distinguishes the transatlantic slave trade from ordinary voluntary migration?

options.text: Africans were forcibly transported and sold into slavery across the Atlantic
Migrants chose their destination and retained equal legal rights
The movement consisted mainly of European scholars travelling to Asia
The trade ended plantation labour in the Americas

explanation: The slave trade was a system of coercion that forcibly transported Africans and subjected them to enslavement and severe suffering.

stem: Which wording about the Gutenberg Bible avoids an inaccurate world-first claim?

options.text: It was the first book printed anywhere in the world
It was the first text ever copied by hand
It was the first major book printed with movable metal type in western Europe
It was the first religious work translated into a vernacular language

explanation: Movable-type printing existed earlier in East Asia. The Gutenberg Bible is accurately described as the first major western European book printed with movable metal type.

stem: Which set of scientist–contribution links is fully correct?

options.text: Vesalius—planetary orbits; Newton—human anatomy; Galileo—blood circulation
Copernicus—heliocentric model; Kepler—elliptical orbits; Harvey—blood circulation

explanation: Copernicus advanced a heliocentric model, Kepler described elliptical planetary orbits, and Harvey studied the circulation of blood.

stem: Which distinction between Vesalius and Harvey is correct?

options.text: Vesalius described gravitation; Harvey published the heliocentric model
Vesalius advanced anatomy through direct study of the body; Harvey explained blood circulation
Vesalius studied planetary orbits; Harvey developed movable-type printing
Vesalius wrote The Prince; Harvey wrote Utopia

explanation: Vesalius’s work focused on human anatomy, while Harvey described the circulation of blood. Their contributions belong to different areas of medicine.

stem: Which complete author–work pairing is correct?

options.text: Erasmus—Utopia; More—The Prince; Machiavelli—In Praise of Folly
Erasmus—In Praise of Folly; More—Utopia; Machiavelli—The Prince
Erasmus—The Last Supper; More—The School of Athens; Machiavelli—David
Erasmus—Principia; More—De revolutionibus; Machiavelli—De motu cordis

explanation: Erasmus, More, and Machiavelli wrote In Praise of Folly, Utopia, and The Prince respectively. The works address different aspects of Renaissance thought.

stem: Which sequence correctly orders the voyages and agreement?

options.text: Dias rounds the Cape (1488) → Columbus crosses the Atlantic (1492) → Tordesillas (1494) → da Gama reaches India by sea (1498)

explanation: Dias rounded the Cape in 1488; Columbus crossed the Atlantic in 1492; Spain and Portugal signed Tordesillas in 1494; da Gama reached India in 1498.

stem: Which conclusion about the first circumnavigation follows from the expedition’s sequence?

options.text: Magellan began the voyage, died before its completion, and Elcano led the return to Spain
Magellan completed the return voyage after Elcano died
Columbus began the voyage and da Gama returned it to Spain
Elcano began the expedition in 1519 and Magellan returned in 1522

explanation: The expedition began under Magellan in 1519. After his death in 1521, Elcano led the surviving crew back to Spain in 1522.
